newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM Q3 operating profits seen plunging.
newsitem.headline: KLM Q3 operating profits seen plunging.

text.p: Third-quarter operating profits at Dutch national carrier KLM Royal Dutch Airlines are set to nosedive, undermined by spiralling fuel and other costs, analysts said on Friday.
But stock watchers are split on how far results could fall when they are announced next Tuesday.
Some believe operating results could plunge into the red from a year-earlier 56 million guilders profit, with estimates ranging from an operating loss of 25 million guilders to a 35 million profit.
Analysts said the rise in costs signalled in the second quarter was likely to continue into the third.
"Fuel costs have soared and pressure on yields will have continued -- particularly in cargo," said Bert van Hoogenhuyze, airlines analyst at broker Amstgeld.
Fuel accounts for some 10 percent of KLM operating costs.
External costs such as landing rights and work by third parties would likely have increased, Van Hoogenhuyze added.
ING Barings' Thibaud de Guerre said he expected fuel costs to come in some 50-75 million guilders higher than the 209 million guilders of the same year-earlier quarter.
Nevertheless total yields were seen roughly in line with last year's, reflecting the stronger dollar, he said.
Higher fuel and salary costs would be the main drag on third-quarter profits, said NIB Strating's Gert Jochems.
"I see fuel costs rising to around 284 million guilders this quarter," he said.
A poor performance at operating level would fall through to the bottom line as KLM has completed the revaluation of its preference stake in U.S. partner Northwest, analysts noted.
The U.S. carrier returned to positive equity in December, which will enable KLM to book its 18.8 percent share of Northwest profits in its final 1996/97 quarter ending March 31.
For now, however, Northwest's contribution to KLM earnings is limited to the dividend and interest on KLM's preferred Northwest shareholding, estimated at four to 16 million guilders.

Analysts were agreed that KLM would not take a restructuring charge in the third quarter, saying its Focus 2000 programme to boost operating results by 1.5 billion guilders over the next three years had so far failed to really take off.
"I've pencilled in a 150 million guilder restructuring charge for this fiscal year, but I think they'll take it in the final quarter," predicted Richard Brakenhoff at MeesPierson.
KLM said last November that it expected full-year net income after tax to fall by 150 million guilders from year-earlier levels before a restructuring provision.
-- Lien van der Leij, A'dam 3120 5045000, Fax 3120 5045040
